title: Chicken and celeriac barley with watercress

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a whole food or a basic staple: chicken, leeks, barley, celeriac, stock, crème fraîche and watercress.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday Tesco item at a normal price.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a lidded casserole plus a knife and board, and browning and simmering are beginner techniques.

works.reason: Eight thighs, 300g pearl barley and 1.2 litres of stock simmered covered for 40 minutes is a sound ratio and timing for four.

honest_times.reason: Peeling and cubing a small celeriac, slicing leeks and browning the chicken fit within 25 minutes, and 45 minutes of cooking matches the 40-minute simmer plus finishing.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including thyme and lemon, is used in the steps, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: The watercress is only stirred through and scattered over at the very end of what is really a chicken and celeriac barley stew, so the hero reads as a finishing green rather than the point of the dish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear British English that a neighbour could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a filling one-pot dinner with protein, wholegrain barley and vegetables that a family would happily eat again.
